title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether the Original Trial Court May Take Litigation Preservation Measures Within the Appeal Period After a First-Instance Judgment

articles.content_en:
Concerning the period for appeal after the first-instance judgment
Reply on Whether the Original Trial Court May Adopt Preservation Measures
Fa (Yan) Fu [1988] No. 7
Higher People's Court of Qinghai Province:
We have received your court's (87) Qing Fa Jing Zi No. 74 'Request for Instructions on Whether the Original Trial Court May Adopt Preservation Measures During the Appeal Period After a First-Instance Judgment.' Upon study, we reply as follows:
When hearing civil cases, the people's court of first instance shall, generally before pronouncing judgment, promptly adopt preservation measures according to law for cases where enforcement of the judgment may be impossible or difficult due to the conduct of the parties or other reasons. If, after pronouncing judgment or during the appeal period following service of the written judgment, it is found that a party has engaged in conduct such as transferring, concealing, selling, or damaging property, and it is deemed necessary to promptly adopt preservation measures, regardless of whether the party has filed an appeal, the people's court of first instance shall adopt preservation measures according to law. However, for appealed cases, the written order on preservation measures made by the court of first instance during the appeal period shall be promptly submitted to the appellate court for filing.
That is the reply.
January 13, 1988
